newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm, unable to pierce resistance.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm, unable to pierce resistance.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted selective gains on Tuesday as activity perked up on minor cash influx, but trade remained range-bound, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 finished up 737.58 points at 63,642.41 after easing from the midday close of 63,788. It had dropped 0.84 percent on Monday after losing 1.7 percent last week mainly due to tension in Iraq.
Daily volume nearly doubled to 6.12 trillion lira from Monday's 3.4 trillion.
"There was minor profit-taking in the afternoon, as was expected after the morning selective buys. Cash entry is still insufficient," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
Reaction buys, mainly in shares of largely state owned stocks, had emerged in the morning after support of the index was confirmed at around 62,500 on Monday.

The market was recently unnerved by a shooting incident in Cyprus, ongoing fighting in northern Iraq and international opposition, particularly from Arab countries to a Turkish plan to set up a security zone there to prevent infiltrations by Kurdish rebels.
A Turkish Cypriot soldier was killed and another was seriously wounded on Sunday when shots were fired at their posts near the U.N.-patrolled buffer zone.
Brokers said the index was likely to continue drifting in narrow ranges unless cash entry increased.

The 85-share industrial index leapt 1.58 percent to 70,157.47 and the 15-share financial index firmed 0.12 percent to 55,668.47. Of the 220 shares traded, gainers outpaced losers by 109 to 44 and 67 were stable.

Actives were led by partially privatised flat steel giant Eregli which gained 500 lira to end at 8,500, largely state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras, also up 500 lira at 14,500 and Turkish Airlines which firmed 1,000 lira to 24,750.
